sources.title: Project Natick
supports: Project Natick was a subsea data-center feasibility research project.
The Phase 2 server failure rate was one-eighth that of the land-based control group.

sources.title: Project Natick Phase 2
supports: The vessel was deployed 117 feet deep off Orkney in June 2018 and operated for two years.
The payload contained 12 racks, 864 servers, and 27.6 petabytes of storage.
The internal environment used dry nitrogen.
Microsoft identified the nitrogen environment and absence of human contact as likely reliability factors.
Project Natick remained a research project rather than a generally available product.

sources.title: Under the sea, Microsoft tests a datacenter
supports: The module was lowered to the seabed using a barge, crane, winches, and a remotely operated vehicle.
The Orkney grid supplied renewable electricity.
The project investigated cold-ocean cooling and lights-out operation.

editorialNotes: Narration is an original synthesis and contains no direct quotation.
The conclusion is framed as interpretation, not as a claim of commercial availability.
No claim is made that underwater data centers are universally superior or environmentally impact-free.
